solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Support for players keeping an eye on the score

definitions.text: Support for players keeping an eye on the score

blocks.note: surface reading: something propping up sportsmen while they watch the match score

blocks.clueFragment: keeping an eye on the score
blocks.note: setter's reading: the players are musicians, and the score is their printed music, held up in front of them

explanation.walkthrough: The score sounds like a match tally and players like a team; really they are an orchestra reading sheet music.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician's stand is the frame that holds the printed music at eye level while an instrumentalist performs.

clue.text: Spice meat and chew oddly

indicators.note: oddly tells us to keep only the letters in odd positions of the words before it, first, third and so on

blocks.note: first and third letters of meat
first and third letters of chew

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: season the meat, then eat it in some odd way.
explanation.definitionFit: Mace is a spice made from the dried red covering of the nutmeg seed.

clue.text: Sword Penny found inside English tower

indicators.note: something found inside another thing sits within it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: steel is a poetic word for a sword
P is the abbreviation for penny
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A sword and a coin are discovered hidden in an English tower.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside STEEL, between its last two letters, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is the tall pointed tower of a church.

clue.text: Stop waffling and teach the scout knots

indicators.note: to knot is to tie up and twist, so the preceding letters are tangled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to a scout leader: stop talking and just show the scout how to tie knots.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut to the chase is an idiom for getting to the point without wasting words.

clue.text: Return to see supporters inside the management

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the word is read from right to left
inside says one piece is placed within the other piece

blocks.note: to spot is to see
bras are garments that support

explanation.surface: Someone goes back to watch their team's fans in the directors' box.
explanation.definitionFit: Top brass is an informal term for the senior officers or executives who run an organisation.

clue.text: Root veg observed growing around back of shop

indicators.note: in a down clue growing means rising upward, so the word is read from bottom to top
the back of a word is its final letter
around says one piece wraps about the other

blocks.note: observed means seen
last letter of shop

explanation.surface: Vegetables are seen sprouting round the back of the greengrocer's.
explanation.walkthrough: Neeps is the Scottish word for turnips or swedes, eaten with haggis.
explanation.definitionFit: Neeps are turnips or swedes, root vegetables, in Scottish usage.

clue.text: Vessel follows small fish

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a cup is a drinking vessel

explanation.surface: A boat trails behind a tiny fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' puts the vessel after the small piece. A scup is a porgy found off the American Atlantic coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The scup is a species of sea bream caught off eastern North America.

clue.text: Bobby left with American composer

blocks.note: a bobby is a British police officer, a cop
L is the abbreviation for left
with means along with, and

explanation.surface: A British policeman went off accompanied by a composer from the US.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is everyday British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron Copland was an American composer known for Appalachian Spring and Fanfare for the Common Man.

clue.text: Leader of regiment cut after exercise but carried on

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: PE is physical education, exercise
first letter of regiment
severed means cut

explanation.surface: A regiment's commander was wounded after drill but kept going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after exercise' places the PE piece first, then the regiment letter and the cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to keep going despite difficulty, so persevered matches carried on in the past tense.

clue.text: Earth found in rabbit's fleece

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: to rabbit is British slang for talking at length, to chat
E is the abbreviation for Earth

explanation.surface: Soil is discovered tangled in a rabbit's fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' is not the animal: in British slang to rabbit (on) is to chatter. 'Fleece' is the verb, not wool.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to swindle them out of money, which is to cheat them.

clue.text: Persuasive leader spotted parking in quay

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: pied means patchy, spotted in two colours
a pier is a landing stage, like a quay
P is the symbol for a car park, parking

explanation.surface: An influential boss was seen leaving his car on the dockside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pied Piper lured away first the rats and then the children of Hamelin, so the name stands for a charismatic leader others follow.

clue.text: Serve under first-rate cabinet-maker?

indicators.note: in a down clue under means placed below, so the serve piece goes second, beneath the first-rate one

blocks.note: prime means top quality
to minister is to serve or attend to

explanation.surface: Work for a top-class furniture craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' puts the serve piece below the first-rate one. The question mark flags that the cabinet is the government's, not a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime minister chooses and appoints the members of the Cabinet, so is literally its maker.

clue.text: Carton rep showed off round wine stall

indicators.note: letters that are shown off are paraded about, so they are thrown into a new arrangement
round says the rearranged letters wrap about the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A packaging salesman showed off at a wine stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stall' looks like a market stand to go with the wine; it is the verb, to play for time.
explanation.definitionFit: To procrastinate is to delay or put off action, which is what stalling means as a verb.

clue.text: Alarming message picked up from reception?

definitions.text: Alarming message picked up from reception?

blocks.note: surface reading: a frightening piece of news
setter's reading: a hotel's front desk rings a guest's room in the morning, acting as an alarm clock

explanation.walkthrough: 'Alarming' suggests scary and 'reception' a radio signal; it is a hotel's morning call to rouse a guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel guest can ask the front desk to phone the room at a set time to rouse them, a service also used figuratively for a jolting warning.

clue.text: Sadly Leo leaves stately home in ruins — it's a gem!

indicators.note: when someone leaves they go away, so those letters are taken out of the phrase
a building in ruins is broken and scattered, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written; these letters are removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Leo departs his crumbling country mansion, and it turns out to be a treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove L, E and O from STATELYHOME and rearrange the eight letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a violet variety of quartz prized as a precious stone.

clue.text: Requirement for an audience will briefly irritate

indicators.note: what is done for an audience is heard rather than read, so we go by sound

blocks.note: a requirement is a need; the whole phrase is then said as one word
will shortened is the contraction 'll, which sounds like this word ending when spoken after need

explanation.surface: A demand made before a crowd will annoy them for a short time.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud, "need'll" (need will) sounds exactly like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to provoke or annoy them with persistent small jibes.

clue.text: Mad Hatter points to cow

indicators.note: mad means crazed and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
N and E are compass points, north and east

explanation.surface: The Mad Hatter from Alice in Wonderland gestures towards a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' looks like the animal; it is the verb meaning to intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them into submission, much as threatening them does.

clue.text: Tempt postponement of hospital department?

blocks.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
a postponed plan is put on ice

explanation.surface: Is putting off a hospital ward's work tempting?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the stretch: putting ENT on ice postpones it, and the result reads ENT then ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure or attract someone by offering something desirable, which is to tempt them.

clue.text: The male carrying gold to sweetheart makes a proposition

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, here taken from sweet
what carries something holds it within, so the outer piece wraps the others

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for male
or is gold in heraldry
central letter of sweet

explanation.surface: A man bringing gold to his beloved makes a proposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proposition' suggests a romantic proposal to go with the sweetheart; in geometry a proposition is a statement to be proved.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a mathematical statement to be proved, which in geometry texts is called a proposition.

clue.text: Famous crime writer's serial killer

blocks.note: first meaning: Agatha ..., the detective novelist
second meaning: John ..., who murdered women at 10 Rillington Place in London

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive, as though the writer owned a killer; it is 'is', joining two people with the same surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to Agatha, the bestselling mystery novelist, and to John Reginald Christie, the notorious 1940s London murderer.

clue.text: Clinical drill good for ocean dweller

blocks.note: a trepan is a surgeon's tool for boring holes in the skull
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A medical boring tool works well for treating a sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A trepang is a sea cucumber, a marine animal eaten dried in East Asian cooking.

clue.text: One into folding paper and leather is an artist

indicators.note: folding bends and creases material out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
into says one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, the and joining the two words
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone into origami and leatherwork counts as an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One into' reads like a hobbyist; it says the numeral goes inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pre-Raphaelites were a Victorian brotherhood of painters such as Rossetti and Millais, so a member is an artist.

clue.text: Animal has endless hunger within

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off
within says one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a yen is a craving or hunger

explanation.surface: A creature is perpetually starving inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' attaches to 'has', not 'hunger': drop its last letter and put the craving between the two left.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is a carnivorous African mammal known for scavenging and its laughing call.

clue.text: Touched fabric

blocks.note: first meaning: past tense of feel, touched with the hand
second meaning: a cloth made of matted wool

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as handling a cloth; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt is the past tense of feel, and also a dense non-woven cloth made by pressing wool fibres together.

clue.text: Wave to entertaining guys after a concert

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them inside your home, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: taken as written
to wave at someone is to greet them
guys are men

explanation.surface: A greeting gesture to some lads having fun after a gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a' puts the A first. 'Concert' is not a gig here but the noun in 'acting in concert'.
explanation.definitionFit: Concert means harmony or accord, as in acting in concert, which is agreement.

clue.text: Kid wants time to rest

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
ease is rest and comfort

explanation.surface: A child needs a moment to have a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' is the verb, to rib someone, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid someone is to tease them, joking at their expense.

clue.text: Old critic getting girl to leave sexy dance

indicators.note: the girl leaving means her name departs from the word, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: the lambada is a sensual Brazilian dance
Ada is a girl's name; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: An elderly reviewer persuades a young woman to walk out of a raunchy dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb was a nineteenth-century English essayist and critic, author of Essays of Elia.

clue.text: In conversation cowboy actor put down wagon maker

indicators.note: in conversation words are spoken and heard, so we go by sound

blocks.note: John Wayne starred in many westerns
to put down on paper is to write

explanation.surface: A western star talking with someone disparaged a cart builder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put down' looks like belittling; it means set down in writing. A wain is an old word for a farm wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A wainwright is a craftsman who builds and repairs wains, the old farm carts.
